name: swap_audit_file
prose: Takes no arguments. It reads the globals lastfile and audit_review_gid (audit_review_gid is only passed along, not assigned) and the cached audit state. It returns -1 if getTSstr fails, and returns -1 if auditd_swap_trail returns any error other than ADE_ACTL (an ADE_ACTL error is only logged and processing continues); on these -1 returns lastfile and the cached state are not changed by this function. If lastfile is non-NULL and its last path component starts with the new timestamp, it logs a debug message and returns 0 before auditd_swap_trail is called, leaving lastfile and the cached state unchanged and closing nothing. Otherwise, if the cached state is AUD_STATE_ENABLED it calls close_lastfile(TS) and ignores the result (close_lastfile can return -1 early if strdup fails, leaving the old trail unrenamed; otherwise it tries to rename lastfile, unlinks the 'current' link only if the rename succeeds, frees lastfile and sets it to NULL); it then sets the cached state to AUD_STATE_ENABLED, calls auditd_new_curlink(newfile) (a failure is only logged), stores newfile in lastfile and returns 0. I did not read the bodies of auditd_swap_trail, auditd_new_curlink or getTSstr.
note: auditd.c:210-275 (swap_audit_file; getTSstr -1 at 217-218, early return 0 at 240, ADE_ACTL check/-1 at 247, close_lastfile 255, assign lastfile 271), close_lastfile 165-205. Reviewer round2 (close_lastfile can return -1 on strdup failure) right: prose now says result ignored and rename may not happen; round15 (audit_review_gid only read) right: prose fixed. Early return 0 at 240 is before any close (original-rejection reviewer claim not in current prose). tt is uninitialised when passed to getTSstr (line 217).

name: wait_for_fd
prose: Takes a descriptor fd and a timeout in seconds (-1 means no timeout is passed to select). It loops: builds an fd_set with only fd, calls select for writability with a fresh timeval each iteration, and if select returns 0 returns ETIMEDOUT; if select returns -1 with errno EINTR it retries the loop (so EINTR is not returned and the timeout restarts from the full value); if select returns -1 with another errno it returns that errno; if select returns a positive count it returns 0 (after PJDLOG_ASSERTs that fd is set). It opens, closes and locks nothing and allocates no memory; behaviour for an fd outside the range an fd_set can hold is not handled by this code.
note: proto_tls.c:112-~145 (select at 127, ETIMEDOUT 130, EINTR retry 133-134, other errno next, success break after the asserts). Reviewer round15 (contract weaker than prose, allows any positive errno) right: contract dropped.

name: receiver_open
prose: Opens or creates the trail file named by filename for the current adhost; it reads and may update adhost->adh_trail_fd and adh_trail_name and renames or opens files through adhost->adh_trail_dirfd. Returns ADIST_ERROR_WRONG_ORDER, leaving everything unchanged, if adh_trail_fd is already not -1 (the previous file was not closed); ADIST_ERROR_INVALID_NAME if trail_validate_name rejects the name; then switches on trail_name_compare(filename, adh_trail_name). TRAIL_RENAMED: if the current trail name is not an unterminated trail it returns ADIST_ERROR_INVALID_NAME, if renameat fails it returns ADIST_ERROR_RENAME, otherwise the file has been renamed on disk and it falls through to the open-existing case. TRAIL_IDENTICAL (and the fall-through): openat with O_WRONLY|O_APPEND|O_NOFOLLOW, ADIST_ERROR_OPEN if it fails (a rename already done is not undone). TRAIL_NEWER: openat with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW mode 0600, ADIST_ERROR_CREATE on failure. TRAIL_OLDER returns ADIST_ERROR_OPEN_OLD; any other compare result aborts via PJDLOG_ABORT. On success it copies filename into adh_trail_name (PJDLOG_VERIFY that it fits), stores the new descriptor in adh_trail_fd and returns 0. On the error returns listed above no new descriptor is stored in adh_trail_fd.
note: receiver.c:276-356: WRONG_ORDER 287, INVALID_NAME 293 and 302, RENAME 311, OPEN 326, CREATE 340, OPEN_OLD 348, abort 350, success 355. Reviewer original (file stays renamed after later failure) right; round15 (WRONG_ORDER state has fd != -1, so not -1) right: prose now says that error leaves state unchanged without claiming fd == -1.

name: auditfilterd_conf_apply
prose: Void. Takes a list of freshly parsed modules and reconciles the global filter_list with it in three passes, matching modules by am_modulename with strcmp. Pass 1: every module in filter_list with no same-named entry in the new list is removed, detached and freed. Pass 2: for every module present in both lists, the argc/argv of the two entries are swapped, auditfilter_module_reinit is called on the old (filter_list) entry; if reinit fails that entry is removed from filter_list, detached and freed, and then the new-list twin is removed from the new list and freed in either case (note the loop then continues from the freed entry's link, a use-after-free if reinit failed). Pass 3: for each remaining new-list entry that is not in filter_list, the entry is removed from the new list and auditfilter_module_attach is called; if attach fails it is freed without a detach, otherwise it is inserted at the head of filter_list (inserting rewrites the entry's list link, so the foreach over the new list then continues through the old filter_list entries, which all match and are skipped, and any later new-list entries are not visited by this pass). Finally if the new list is still non-empty it only warns. So after the call filter_list is not guaranteed to equal the new configuration: modules whose reinit or attach failed are absent, and entries skipped by the pass 3 iteration quirk stay in the new list.
note: auditfilterd_conf.c:345-461 (pass1 355-375, pass2 383-427, reinit at 412, reinit failure frees am1 at 415-417 then the foreach continues, pass3 attach at 451, TAILQ_INSERT_HEAD at 456, non-empty warning 459-460). Reviewer original (filter_list may lack modules from new list after reinit/attach failures) right; round15 (attach-failed modules freed without detach) right: prose says so. Pass 3 skipping later entries is my own reading of TAILQ_INSERT_HEAD overwriting am_list.tqe_next (not tested).

name: main
prose: Program entry of auditreduce; slice cut the head. It parses options "Aa:b:c:d:e:f:g:j:m:o:r:u:vz:" with getopt, recording options in opttochk. For -a, -b it uses strptime/mktime on the argument; -d sets both the start and end time of that day and rejects use together with -a or -b by calling usage; for -a/-b the usage call is made if the same option repeats. For -e, -f, -g, -r, -u a non-numeric argument is looked up as a user or group name and, if the lookup fails, the option is silently skipped (break) without setting its flag. -c calls usage if getauditflagsbin fails; -m grows the p_evec array (32 entries initially, doubling) and exits with err(1) if malloc or realloc fails, and calls usage if the argument is neither a number nor a known event name; unknown options call usage. With no file operands it optionally (HAVE_CAP_ENTER) calls cap_enter (exiting with EXIT_FAILURE on failure other than ENOSYS), runs select_records(stdin), exits with errx(EXIT_FAILURE) if that returns -1 and otherwise exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). With file operands it opens each file (errx EXIT_FAILURE if fopen fails); in a HAVE_CAP_ENTER build it forks a child that cap_enters and runs select_records and the parent waits and exits EXIT_FAILURE if the child's exit status is nonzero (the fork result is not checked); otherwise it runs select_records in-process with errx(EXIT_FAILURE) on -1; then fclose, and after all files exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). It does not return normally. I did not read select_records, usage or parse_object_type.
note: auditreduce.c:636-879 (slice 777-879 only covers the tail; options 658-818, stdin branch 824-832, file loop 838-876, exit 878). Reviewer round15 (parent exits EXIT_FAILURE directly for nonzero child status) right (line 869-870). Name-outside-slice complaint was a slice cut, function is main at 636.

name: EtmV3PktProcImpl::OnISyncPacket
prose: Void. Builds the current ETMv3 I-sync packet from m_currPacketData, starting with m_currPktIdx set to 1 (its previous value is discarded). If m_bIsync_got_cycle_cnt is set it reads a cycle count with extractCycleCount, stores it and marks the I-sync as having a cycle count. If m_config.CtxtIDBytes() is non-zero it reads the context ID with extractCtxtID and updates it. Then it reads one info byte: bits 6:5 give the I-sync reason, bit 3 updates the NS flag, bit 1 updates the Hyp flag only if hasVirtExt(), bit 4 is J, and bit 2 is AltISA only if MinorRev() >= 3 (otherwise AltISA is 0). If isInstrTrace() it reads four bytes little endian as the instruction address, takes bit 0 as the T flag, clears it, updates the 32-bit address, sets ISA to jazelle if J, else to tee if T and AltISA, else to thumb2 if T, else to arm; if m_bIsync_get_LSiP_addr is also set it reads a branch-style address with extractBrAddrPkt and updates the data address first with the main address (32 bits) then with the LSiP address (LSiPBits bits). If isInstrTrace() is false it marks the packet as having no address (no address or ISA update). Finally it calls SendPacket(). m_currPktIdx is left after the consumed bytes; the function does not bounds-check the data it indexes. I did not read extractCycleCount, extractCtxtID or extractBrAddrPkt.

Reviewer original (address/ISA only if isInstrTrace; incoming m_currPktIdx irrelevant) right; prose reworded without the precondition.

name: TrcPktDecodeEtmV4I::processException
prose: Returns an ocsd_err_t. It takes the exception element off the back of m_P0_stack (a TrcStackElemExcept is assumed, not checked) and pops it. If the exception came from the ETE PE-reset packet it skips the address handling; otherwise it looks at the next element, pops it if it is a context element (remembering it), and requires the following element to be an address element: if it is not, it returns the result of handlePacketSeqErr(OCSD_ERR_BAD_PACKET_SEQ, ...) with the popped elements still pending deletion. The address element itself is read but not popped. If the exception's previous-same flag (branch target) is set, the current instruction address and ISA (aarch64 or arm from the context SF bit or current ISA; thumb2 if the address element's ISA is nonzero) are set from the address and m_need_addr is cleared. It then adds an output element (returns that error if addElem fails); if a context element was found it calls updateContext into it (return value ignored) and adds another element. Unless this was a PE reset, if the current instruction address differs from the return address it calls traceInstrToWP: on error it returns that error (additionally setting m_need_addr and m_need_ctxt and logging a warning for OCSD_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ISA, or logging an error for other codes); a found waypoint, or a partial range with different start and end, yields a trace-range element (followed by a new element), and a missing waypoint sets m_need_addr; if the walk reported inaccessible memory it fills an ADDR_NACC element at the current address and adds another element. Finally it fills the current element as OCSD_GEN_TRC_ELEM_EXCEPTION with its end address set to the return address (0 for PE reset), its exception-return-address flag set to 1, the branch-target flag and the exception number, calls m_P0_stack.delete_popped() and returns the last value of err (OCSD_OK at that point, because each addElem or traceInstrToWP failure returns before this line). Error returns leave popped elements undeleted.
note: trc_pkt_decode_etmv4i.cpp:1392-1550 (exception pop 1406-1411, ETE reset check 1409, ctxt 1417-1422, address missing 1424-1431, branch target 1440-1455, addElem 1460, updateContext 1466 ignored, traceInstrToWP 1482-1497, NACC 1527-1536, exception element 1540-1546, delete_popped 1548). Reviewer round2 (updateContext result unchecked) right, prose says ignored; round1 (contract weaker, UNSUPPORTED_ISA path) right, no contract given. I did not read traceInstrToWP, handlePacketSeqErr or updateContext bodies.

name: TrcPktProcEtmV4I::onReset
prose: If m_isInit is false it returns OCSD_RESP_FATAL_NOT_INIT and changes nothing. Otherwise it calls InitProcessorState and returns OCSD_RESP_CONT. InitProcessorState clears the buffered packet data (m_currPacketData), calls initNextPacket on the current packet, sets m_update_on_unsync_packet_index to 0, sets the packet function to iNotSync, the packet index to 0, m_is_sync, m_first_trace_info and m_sent_notsync_packet to false, m_process_state to PROC_HDR and calls initStartState on the current packet.

name: TrcPktProcEtmV4I::onFlush
prose: If m_isInit is false it returns OCSD_RESP_FATAL_NOT_INIT; otherwise it returns OCSD_RESP_CONT. In both cases it changes no member state and does not look at or emit any buffered packet data (the code comment says full packets are sent immediately and only a partial packet may be pending).

name: TrcPktProcEtmV4I::BuildIPacketTable
prose: Void. Fills the 256-entry m_i_table: all entries are first set to ETM4_PKT_I_RESERVED with the iPktReserved handler, then the header bytes that have defined packets get their pkt_type and handler (extension, trace info, timestamp, exception, cycle count, speculation, conditional, event, context, address, Q and atom packets and others). Several entries depend on m_config: 0x05 (function return) gets the no-payload handler only for a Cortex-M profile with a v8 architecture and FullVersion >= 0x42, otherwise its handler stays iPktReserved; 0x07 (exception return) gets iPktNoPayload for MajVersion < 5, and for MajVersion >= 5 gets either the ignore type with the no-payload handler (if ETE_TRACE_ERET_AS_IGNORE is defined at compile time) or iPktInvalidCfg (if not); with MajVersion >= 5, 0x0A and 0x0B get the transaction start/commit types and 0x09 the ITE packet only if MinVersion >= 3; entries 0x70 (ignore) need FullVersion >= 0x43, 0x88 (timestamp marker) FullVersion >= 0x46, and 0xB0-0xB9 (source address packets) FullVersion >= 0x50; Q packets are enabled only if hasQElem(), with certain Q type codes left reserved; many data-trace and conditional-trace entries use iPktInvalidCfg when their feature is not enabled. It returns nothing and has no failure path. Partly read: I only checked the middle table entries (about 1344-1500) and the atom loops by pattern, not entry by entry.
note: trc_pkt_proc_etmv4i.cpp:1271-1658 (name in packet was InitITable, not in the file). 0x05 at 1299-1306, 0x07 at 1312-1324, ETE packets 1326-1342, 0x70 at 1503-1508, 0x88 at 1538-1543, Q 1571-1591, 0xB0-0xB9 at 1593-1615. Reviewer round17 (ETE_TRACE_ERET_AS_IGNORE path makes 0x07 ignore, not invalid-config) right (1316-1321).

name: TrcPktProcEtmV4I::iPktCycleCntF123
prose: Void. Called for each byte of a cycle-count packet with the newest byte in lastByte; it uses m_curr_packet.type (F1, F2 or F3) and the number of bytes in m_currPacketData. When the packet has 1 byte it first sets m_count_done and m_commit_done to false and m_has_count to true; then for F3 it sets the commit-element count to bits 3:2 of the byte plus 1 only if commitOpt1 is false, sets the cycle count to getCCThreshold() plus bits 1:0, and sets m_process_state to SEND_PKT; for F1 with bit 0 set it clears m_has_count and sets m_count_done, and if commitOpt1 is true it sets m_commit_done (F2 with one byte only gets the flag reset). When the packet is F2 with 2 bytes it sets the cycle count to getCCThreshold() plus bits 3:0, the commit-element count to bits 7:4 plus (MaxSpecDepth-15 if bit 0 is set, else 1), and SEND_PKT. Otherwise (any other size, F1 continuation bytes) it sets m_commit_done from the cleared bit 7 if commit is not yet done, else m_count_done likewise. After that, for F1 only, if both m_commit_done and m_count_done are set it parses the buffer: if commitOpt1 is false it extracts a commit field from index 1 and sets the commit elements; if m_has_count it extracts the count field and sets the cycle count to that value plus getCCThreshold(), else sets the cycle count to 0; and sets SEND_PKT. Otherwise the cycle count and process state are left unchanged.
note: trc_pkt_proc_etmv4i.cpp:602-675 (size 1 at 606-634, F3 611-621 (commit +1 at 616), F2 635-646, else 647-654, F1 completion 656-674). Reviewer original (F1 with commitOpt1 true completes without setting commit elements) right, prose says commit only set if !commitOpt1; round15 (F3 commit is bits 3:2 plus 1) right, fixed.

name: T_FUNC(empty_policy, "empty policy")
prose: Generated function t_empty_policy_func (static, from the T_FUNC macro; both arguments are unused). It creates a temporary policy file containing only the comment line "# empty policy", calls pam_start on it with a scripted conversation, and if pam_start does not return PAM_SUCCESS it prints the code and returns 0 without closing the temporary file or calling pam_end. Otherwise it calls pam_authenticate, pam_setcred, pam_acct_mgmt, pam_chauthtok, pam_open_session and pam_close_session with flags 0, prints each result, and returns nonzero only if all six returned PAM_SYSTEM_ERR (the results are ANDed). Before returning it calls pam_end with the last status and closes the temporary file.

name: T_FUNC(mod_return, "module return value")
prose: Generated function t_mod_return_func (static, from the T_FUNC macro; arguments unused). For each entry of the static table t_pam_return_cases (currently one entry: PAM_AUTH facility, PAM_SM_AUTHENTICATE, two PAM_REQUIRED modules both returning PAM_SUCCESS) it creates a temporary policy file with two lines of the form "facility control-flag pam_return_so error=name" (pam_return_so comes from the PAM_RETURN_SO environment variable), calls pam_start on it, and if that fails prints the code, closes the file and moves to the next case. Otherwise it calls the pam primitive selected by the table's primitive field (a switch without a default, so pam_err keeps its pam_start value for an unknown primitive), prints its return value, calls pam_end, prints "here" and closes the file. It then returns 1 whether or not the primitive's result matched the table's result field, which the function does not read (nothing in its body compares against it).

name: pamk5_authenticate
prose: Takes args and returns a PAM status; slice cut the head and the real function is pamk5_authenticate, not pam_sm_authenticate. If use_authtok is set without force_first_pass it logs an error and sets force_first_pass. It calls pamk5_context_new (any non-success status is returned through the exit code, which calls pamk5_context_free), and returns PAM_USER_UNKNOWN if pamk5_should_ignore says to ignore the user. It then calls pamk5_password_auth. If that returns PAM_NEW_AUTHTOK_REQD: with fail_pwchange it becomes PAM_AUTH_ERR; with defer_pwchange it sets ctx->expired and becomes PAM_SUCCESS; with force_pwchange it prints an info message, moves PAM_AUTHTOK into PAM_OLDAUTHTOK when available, clears PAM_AUTHTOK, sets use_first_pass and returns the result of pamk5_password_change; with none of those flags the status PAM_NEW_AUTHTOK_REQD is kept. Any status other than PAM_SUCCESS is logged and returned. It then calls pamk5_authorized (non-success returned), sets PAM_USER to ctx->name unless expired or no_update_user (errors only logged), logs the authentication, and calls pam_set_data("pam_krb5", ctx, pamk5_context_destroy): on failure it logs, calls pamk5_context_free and returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR (the common exit code then calls pamk5_context_free again; I did not check whether that second call is a harmless no-op). On success it records that the context is stored, and unless no_ccache is set or the context is expired it returns the result of pamk5_cache_init_random with the obtained credentials. At the exit label the credentials are freed only if both creds and ctx are non-NULL; args->ctx is set to NULL only if the context was stored; and on any non-success status the stored context is cleared with pam_set_data(NULL) if this call stored it, otherwise pamk5_context_free is called.
note: auth.c:976-1141 (head 976-984; context_new 994; ignore 1000-1003; password_auth/expired handling 1041-1065; authorized 1072; PAM_USER 1079-1083; pam_set_data 1098-1104; cache init 1112-1113; done: 1115-1140). Name in packet was pam_sm_authenticate (tail); the function in the file is pamk5_authenticate. Reviewer round17 (credentials freed only when creds and ctx are non-NULL, not always) right (1116); previous prose said always.

name: pamk5_password
prose: Takes args and only_auth and returns a PAM status. If ignore_root is set or minimum_uid > 0 and pam_get_user succeeds and pamk5_should_ignore says to ignore that user, it returns PAM_IGNORE; before that, only when only_auth is false, it frees and clears the configured banner and calls pamk5_password_prompt (result ignored), and with only_auth true it touches neither. Otherwise, if args->config->ctx is NULL it calls pamk5_context_new and registers the new context with pam_set_data("pam_krb5", ..., pamk5_context_destroy): either failure returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR, and on a pam_set_data failure the newly created context is left in args->config->ctx unregistered and not freed here; on success it records the context as registered and sets args->ctx to NULL at exit. If the context is expired and has no creds and neither force_first_pass nor use_first_pass is set it shows a "Password expired" message. It then returns the result of pamk5_password_change(args, only_auth) immediately when only_auth is true; otherwise, if that succeeded and the context is expired, it sets force_first_pass, calls pamk5_password_auth (a non-success status is returned), logs the principal, clears ctx->expired, returns the result of pamk5_cache_init_random and frees the credentials. In all exits a non-success status of PAM_SERVICE_ERR, PAM_AUTH_ERR or PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL is changed to PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR and other statuses are returned unchanged. The local pass buffer is never assigned, so its cleanup does nothing.
note: password.c:271-401 (ignore 292-305, banner free only inside !only_auth at 295-301, context creation 311-326, expired message 337-340, change 346-348, expired follow-up 355-379, done 381-400). Reviewer original (pam_set_data failure leaves context created but unregistered) right; round15 (banner freed only when only_auth is false) right: prose now states it.

name: LOG_FUNCTION(crit,   LOG_CRIT)
prose: Generated function putil_crit(pargs, fmt, ...), a printf-style logger at priority LOG_CRIT. It starts a va_list, calls log_vplain(pargs, LOG_CRIT, fmt, args) and ends the va_list; it returns nothing. log_vplain does not suppress messages at this priority; with pargs non-NULL and pargs->user set it formats the message and logs "(user NAME) MSG" via pam_syslog, with pargs non-NULL and no user it uses pam_vsyslog on pargs->pamh, and with pargs NULL it formats the message and logs it with syslog and LOG_AUTHPRIV (a formatting failure logs a critical syslog line and drops the message).
note: logging.c:174-193 (macro), 194 (invocation), log_vplain 100-122, format 82-92.

name: LOG_FUNCTION(err,    LOG_ERR)
prose: Generated function putil_err(pargs, fmt, ...), the same as putil_crit but at priority LOG_ERR: it calls log_vplain(pargs, LOG_ERR, fmt, args) and returns nothing. The message is logged through pam_syslog (with a "(user NAME) " prefix when pargs->user is set), pam_vsyslog when pargs has no user, or plain syslog with LOG_AUTHPRIV when pargs is NULL; no priority filtering happens at this level.
note: logging.c:174-193, 195, log_vplain 100-122.

It starts a va_list and calls log_pam(pargs, LOG_CRIT, status, fmt, args), returns nothing. log_pam formats the message (and returns silently after a critical syslog line if formatting fails); with pargs NULL it logs the message via log_plain with no PAM error text; with pargs non-NULL it logs the message alone if status is PAM_SUCCESS, otherwise the message followed by ": " and pam_strerror(pargs->pamh, status), and frees the formatted message.

name: test_print_range
prose: Prints a number range to stdout and returns a count. With first, last, chars (characters already on the line) and limit it first computes needed: the decimal digits of first (0 digits if first is 0), plus, only if last > first, the digits of last plus 1, plus 2 if chars > 0. If limit > 0 and chars + needed > limit: if chars <= limit it prints ", " (only when chars > 0) followed by "..." and returns 5 when chars > 0 or 3 when chars == 0; if chars > limit it prints nothing and returns 0. Otherwise (limit is 0 or the text fits) it prints ", " when chars > 0, then "first-" when last > first, then last, and returns needed. When last < first it prints only last but the returned count is the digit count of first (plus 2 if chars > 0), so the return value equals the printed length only when last >= first or the digit counts match.
note: runtests.c:946-980 (needed 953-961, limit branch 962-971, normal print 972-978). Reviewer round1 (returns digits(first) when last < first) right; round2 mixed; round15 (contract omits printf) right: contract removed since the function writes to stdout.

name: pam_sm_chauthtok
prose: Takes pamh, flags, argc, argv and returns a PAM status. It copies the default params and calls parse (a non-success status is returned). flags must contain PAM_PRELIM_CHECK or PAM_UPDATE_AUTHTOK, otherwise it returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR; the matching ask-old-password option (prelim or update) decides whether to ask. If asking and getuid() != 0 it prompts for the old password and stores it with pam_set_item(PAM_OLDAUTHTOK) (any failure, or an empty reply giving PAM_AUTHTOK_RECOVERY_ERR, is returned). With PAM_PRELIM_CHECK it then returns the current status (PAM_SUCCESS here) without choosing or setting any new password. Otherwise it fetches PAM_USER and PAM_OLDAUTHTOK (failures returned), builds a fake passwd for non-UNIX users or calls getpwnam (PAM_USER_UNKNOWN if the user does not exist) and, if the check-old-password option is set and getuid() != 0, verifies oldpass against the password or shadow hash with crypt (PAM_AUTH_ERR if oldpass is missing or does not match); in the getpwnam case it zeroes pw_passwd afterwards and returns any error status. With the use_authtok option it reads PAM_AUTHTOK and returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR if it is missing or too long under enforcement, runs the strength check and, if the password is weak, says so and returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR only when enforcement applies (the say result is ignored), and on this branch it does not set a new token. Otherwise it loops: it prints introduction/explanation messages (a failed say there is returned), generates a random password (if generation fails and only random passwords are allowed it says so, ignoring the say result, and returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR; a failed say about the random password only discards it), prompts for the new password (failure or empty reply returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR after wiping the random password; if strdup fails it returns the current status, which is PAM_SUCCESS at that point, without setting anything), checks length and strength (with enforcement failures set PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR and request a retry; messages from say are ignored), prompts a second time and compares (a mismatch prints a message and gives PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR with a retry only if the say succeeded; an empty reply gives PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR), and on success calls pam_set_item(PAM_AUTHTOK, newpass), whose result becomes the status. It overwrites the typed and random passwords and frees newpass. If a retry was requested and retries remain it says the retry message and loops if that say succeeded, otherwise returns the say status; the final return is the current status.
note: pam_passwdqc.c:310-554 (flags 333-341, old password 343-361, user/oldpass items 363-371, check old 373-407, use_authtok 416-430, loop 434-551 with strdup failure return status at 497-500, retry at 547-551). Reviewer original (PRELIM_CHECK and use_authtok can return PAM_SUCCESS without setting a new token) right; round15 (some say() failures ignored) right (479, 513/515, 425). I did not read parse, converse, say, check_max or _passwdqc_check.

name: isolation_protocol
prose: Takes no arguments and returns an int. It calls send_Initiation_LFSR, writes 0x04 to PNP_CONFIG_CONTROL (reset the CSN of all cards), then loops csn from 1 while csn < PNP_MAX_CARDS: each iteration sets the global logdevs to 0, writes PNP_WAKE 0, writes the global rd_port to PNP_SET_RD_DATA, writes PNP_SERIAL_ISOLATION to the address port, busy-waits about 1 ms with DELAY(1000), then calls get_serial(data); if it succeeds it calls dump_resdata(data, csn) (which sets logdevs for that card and, per the reviewer, mallocs and frees resource buffers; I did not read dump_resdata beyond locating malloc/free at pnpinfo.c:495-514), and if it fails the loop breaks. It returns csn - 1: the number of iterations that succeeded before the first get_serial failure, or PNP_MAX_CARDS - 1 if none failed. On return logdevs is 0 if the loop ended on a get_serial failure, else the value left by the last dump_resdata. The function itself allocates nothing and takes no locks.
note: pnpinfo.c:555-579 (logdevs reset 567, get_serial 573-576, return 578); dump_resdata 470, malloc/free 495-514. Reviewer round2 (logdevs 0 after a failed later card) right; round15 (dump_resdata mallocs/frees) right; original/round1 contract complaints moot (contract removed, function uses globals and I/O).

name: cnd_wait
prose: Static inline wrapper in the POSIX threads shim. If cnd or mtx is NULL it returns thrd_error. Otherwise it calls pthread_cond_wait(&cnd->cond, &mtx->mutex) (which releases the mutex while waiting and reacquires it before returning, and may wake spuriously) and returns thrd_error if that call returned a nonzero error code, else thrd_success. It allocates or frees nothing.
note: threads.h:245-257 (NULL check 249-250, pthread_cond_wait 252, returns 254 and 256). Reviewer round15 (claims NULL check absent, code dereferences without it) wrong: the check exists at line 249. Name-outside-slice complaints were due to the slice cut.

name: pt_blk_event
prose: Returns -pte_invalid if decoder or uevent is NULL and -pte_bad_query if decoder->process_event is clear. Otherwise it switches on the type of decoder->event: enabled sets variant.enabled.resumed when decoder->ip equals the event ip and calls pt_blk_process_enabled; async_disabled returns -pte_bad_query unless decoder->ip equals variant.async_disabled.at (this check does not look at ip_suppressed) and then, like disabled, calls pt_blk_process_disabled; async_branch returns -pte_bad_query unless decoder->ip equals variant.async_branch.from (also without checking ip_suppressed) and calls pt_blk_process_async_branch; async_paging, async_vmcs, exec_mode and tsx return -pte_bad_query when the event ip is not suppressed and does not match decoder->ip, then call the paging, vmcs, exec_mode or tsx process function (paging and vmcs events themselves skip the check); overflow and stop call their process functions; exstop and mwait return -pte_bad_query on an IP mismatch (only when the ip is not suppressed and the decoder is enabled) and otherwise clear process_event; pwre, pwrx, ptwrite, tick, cbr and mnt just clear process_event; an event type with no case falls out of the switch unchanged. Any negative status from a process function is returned immediately, before the event is copied to the user. After the switch it copies min(size, sizeof(event)) bytes of the event to uevent and returns the result of pt_blk_proceed_trailing_event(decoder, NULL) (a status or negative error; I did not read it). The process_* helpers are not read here, so whether they clear process_event is not claimed.
note: pt_block_decoder.c:3321-3473 (argument checks 3327-3332, async_disabled 3350-3352, async_branch 3363-3365, paging/vmcs 3373-3397, exec_mode/tsx 3406-3423, exstop/mwait 3434-3448, copy 3466-3469, return 3472). Reviewer round15 (async_disabled/async_branch IP checks ignore ip_suppressed) right; original (omits IP-match and -pte_bad_query paths) right.

name: pt_df_fetch
prose: Selects the decoder function for the packet at pos. It returns -pte_internal if dfun or config is NULL; otherwise it sets *dfun to NULL first (so *dfun is NULL on the -pte_nosync and -pte_eos returns below). It returns -pte_nosync if pos is NULL, before config->begin or after config->end, and -pte_eos if pos equals config->end. It reads the opcode byte and picks a static decoder function, storing it in *dfun and returning 0: masked opcodes tnt_8, cyc, tip, fup, tip_pge and tip_pgd (checked in that order), pad, mode, tsc, mtc, otherwise pt_decode_unknown. For the extended opcode it returns -pte_eos if there is no following byte, then selects on that byte: ptw (masked), psb, ovf, tnt_64, psbend, cbr, pip, tma, stop, vmcs, exstop (either form), mwait, pwre, pwrx, or pt_decode_unknown for others; for ext2 it returns -pte_eos if the next byte is missing and selects mnt or pt_decode_unknown. It reads only the input bytes, writes only *dfun, and allocates nothing.
note: pt_decoder_function.c:220-379 (function is pt_df_fetch; slice cut the head, packet name pt_decode_opcode does not exist). Checks 226-239, opcode switch 242-293, ext 294-377, ext2 363-376.

name: pt_enc_next
prose: Slice shows only the first half of pt_enc_next. Encodes one packet into the encoder's buffer: it returns -pte_invalid if encoder or packet is NULL; otherwise it switches on packet->type. For most types it first calls pt_reserve (a negative result, for example -pte_eos when the packet does not fit before config.end or -pte_internal if encoder->pos is NULL, is returned and nothing is written), writes the bytes at encoder->pos, stores the advanced position in encoder->pos and returns the number of bytes written. Types fup, tip, tip_pge and tip_pgd return the result of pt_encode_ip. tnt_8 returns -pte_bad_packet if bit_size >= 7, checked before pt_reserve. tnt_64 calls pt_reserve first and then returns -pte_invalid if bit_size >= pt_pl_tnt_64_bits or the payload has bits at or above the stop bit. mode returns -pte_bad_packet after the reservation for a leaf other than exec or tsx. tma returns -pte_bad_packet after the reservation if fc has bits outside pt_pl_tma_fc_mask. cyc returns -pte_bad_packet before the reservation if the value needs more than pt_pl_cyc_max_size bytes. ptw returns pt_ptw_size's negative error before the reservation. ppt_unknown, ppt_invalid and any unlisted type return -pte_bad_opc. encoder->pos is only assigned just before a successful return, so on the error returns made by this function itself it is unchanged and no bytes are published (pt_encode_ip's own behaviour was not read).
note: pt_encoder.c:249-690 (function starts at 249; the packet name pt_encode_packet does not exist). NULL check 254, tnt_8 324-341, tnt_64 344-365, mode 368-404, tma 454-474, cyc 488-526 (bad_packet at 505-506), ptw 655-682, bad_opc 684-689; pt_reserve 141-161. The first-half slice is 254-507; I read the whole function.

name: pt_enc_next
prose: Encodes one packet into the encoder's buffer and returns the number of bytes written (positive) on success, or a negative error code. It returns -pte_invalid if encoder or packet is NULL. The caller does not need to reserve space: each packet case calls pt_reserve itself, and returns its negative result (-pte_eos if the bytes would pass config.end, -pte_internal if encoder->pos is NULL) without writing. The packet types pad, psb, psbend, ovf, tnt_8, tnt_64, mode, pip, tsc, cbr, tma, mtc, cyc, stop, vmcs, mnt, exstop, mwait, pwre, pwrx and ptw write their opcode and payload bytes at encoder->pos; fup, tip, tip_pge and tip_pgd return pt_encode_ip's result. Invalid payloads: tnt_8 bit_size >= 7 gives -pte_bad_packet (before the reservation); tnt_64 with bit_size >= pt_pl_tnt_64_bits or payload bits at or above the stop bit gives -pte_invalid (after the reservation; not -pte_bad_packet); a mode leaf other than exec or tsx gives -pte_bad_packet; tma fc outside pt_pl_tma_fc_mask gives -pte_bad_packet; a cyc value needing more than pt_pl_cyc_max_size bytes gives -pte_bad_packet; a ptw plc for which pt_ptw_size is negative returns that negative value; ppt_unknown, ppt_invalid and any other type give -pte_bad_opc. encoder->pos is advanced only on the success path, so it stays unchanged on the error returns made by this function itself (pt_encode_ip's own behaviour was not read).
note: pt_encoder.c:249-690 (reserve in each case, e.g. 260, 272, 330, 347; tnt_64 -pte_invalid at 351-358; ptw 655-681; bad_opc 684-689). Reviewer original (no pre-reservation needed) right; round15 (TNT-64 invalid size gives -pte_bad_packet) wrong: lines 351-358 return -pte_invalid, prose keeps it.

name: pt_insn_event
prose: Returns -pte_invalid if decoder or uevent is NULL and -pte_bad_query if decoder->process_event is clear. It switches on decoder->event.type: any type not listed below returns -pte_bad_query. enabled sets variant.enabled.resumed when decoder->ip equals the event ip and calls pt_insn_process_enabled; async_disabled returns -pte_bad_query when the ip is not suppressed and does not equal variant.async_disabled.at, and then (like disabled) calls pt_insn_process_disabled; async_branch returns -pte_bad_query unless decoder->ip equals variant.async_branch.from and calls pt_insn_process_async_branch; async_paging and async_vmcs check the ip (when not suppressed) and, like paging and vmcs, call their process function; overflow, exec_mode, tsx and stop call their process functions; exstop and mwait return -pte_bad_query on an IP mismatch when the ip is not suppressed and decoder->enabled is set; pwre, pwrx, ptwrite, tick, cbr and mnt do nothing special. A negative status from a process function or an IP-mismatch return leaves decoder->process_event set, since it is cleared only after the event copy. Then it copies min(size, sizeof(event)) bytes to uevent, clears decoder->process_event, and if decoder->process_insn is set calls pt_insn_check_insn_event (negative status returned; a status with pts_event_pending returned) and then pt_insn_proceed_postponed (negative status returned). It finally returns the result of pt_insn_check_ip_event(decoder, NULL, NULL). I did not read the process helpers.
note: pt_insn_decoder.c:1592-1769 (checks 1598-1603, default bad_query 1607-1613, async_disabled 1629-1632, switch to 1727, copy 1735-1738, process_event cleared 1741, insn events 1749-1765, final return 1768). Reviewer original (process_event not cleared on early validation errors) right; round15 (prose said it stays set on the no-pending-event error although the code returns when it is clear) right: prose rewritten.

name: apl12_resume_disabled
prose: Static helper for erratum APL12 that replays packets from the query decoder's position to the resume point offset bytes ahead, then resumes with tracing treated as disabled. Returns -pte_internal if decoder is NULL; gets the current offset with pt_qry_get_offset and syncs pkt to it with pt_pkt_sync_set (negative results returned). It then loops reading packets with pt_pkt_next and the offset after each with pt_pkt_get_offset: if reading a packet fails with -pte_eos it returns 0 without advancing decoder->pos and without creating an event (timing state may already have been updated by earlier replayed packets); other read/offset errors are returned; when the offset after a packet reaches begin+offset it stops (returning -pte_internal if it jumped past it). For each packet before that point, mode, pip and vmcs packets give -pte_internal, tsc, cbr, tma, mtc and cyc packets are applied to decoder->time and decoder->tcal with pt_qry_apply_* (a negative result is returned), and all others are skipped. After the loop it does decoder->pos += offset and returns pt_qry_event_ovf_disabled(decoder), which prepares a standalone overflow event with ip_suppressed set, clears decoder->enabled, stores it in decoder->event and returns -pte_internal if no event could be allocated or otherwise the result of pt_qry_event_time (not read, so its sign is not claimed).
note: pt_query_decoder.c:2400-2526 (eos return 2426-2429, past-offset check 2444-2449, internal for mode/pip/vmcs 2456-2464, apply cases 2466-2519, advance and return 2523-2525); pt_qry_event_ovf_disabled 1840-1863. Reviewer original (EOS path returns 0 without advancing) right; round15 (return may not be positive) unproven because pt_qry_event_time was not read; prose no longer states a sign.

name: pt_time_update_mtc
prose: Updates the timing state from an MTC packet. Returns -pte_internal if time, packet or config is NULL (nothing changed). If time->have_tsc is set and time->have_tma is clear it returns 0 with no state changed. Otherwise it computes ctc = (uint32_t)packet->ctc << config->mtc_freq; sets time->ctc_cyc to ctc if time->fc or time->lost_cyc was nonzero or time->have_mtc was clear at entry; sets time->have_mtc to 1, time->fc to 0, time->ctc to ctc and time->lost_cyc to 0. Then: if have_mtc was clear at entry and have_tma is clear it returns 0 (tsc and base unchanged); if have_mtc was clear at entry and have_tma is set and the entry value of time->ctc has bits outside pt_pl_tma_ctc_mask it returns -pte_internal (tsc and base unchanged); on the first MTC with a TMA seen it extends the previous ctc with estimated high bits from this MTC. It then calls pt_time_ctc_delta; on failure it increments time->lost_mtc and returns that error. It calls pt_time_ctc_fc; on failure it returns that error without touching lost_mtc. On success it sets time->base and time->tsc to the entry base plus the computed TSC delta and returns 0. Because have_mtc, fc, ctc and lost_cyc are written before the later checks, those fields are already changed on the error returns after that point.
note: pt_time.c:234-339 (NULL check 243-244, have_tsc && !have_tma early return 256-257, field updates 266-275, first MTC branch 280-323, delta 325-329, fc 331-333, result 335-338). Reviewer round15 (code has no early return when have_tsc set and have_tma clear) wrong: lines 256-257 do exactly that; prose unchanged in substance.
